question: Are the two construction-holdout control flips introduced by the MLP0 hidden split, or inherited from the full five-MLP parent intervention?
population: The identical 16 temporal-v13/is-was-v12 C controls from the holdout; no control-family substitution.

predictions.pred_a_authority_replay_finiteness_and_p: Holdout hash/terminal match; mask30 aggregate controls replay within 1e-6; all per-row metrics finite; observed forwards <=20.
predictions.pred_b_mask30_adds_no_collateral_over_fu: Every mask30 top-1 flip is also a full-parent flip, mask30 median KL is <= full median KL +.002, and each task margin-RMS fraction is <= full +.02.
predictions.pred_c_full_parent_explains_the_failed_a: The full parent flips at least the same two rows as mask30.
predictions.pred_d_top50_exposes_the_function_select: All-top50 has fewer flips or lower median KL than mask30, while the authority shows at least .03 less temporal target behavior.
predictions.pred_e_mask30_and_full_control_effects_a: Centered mask30-minus-full logit RMS is <=5% of centered full-minus-base RMS.

terminal_policy.parent_limited_selectivity: A-E pass: the internal MLP0 split transfers without extra collateral, but the full parent itself fails this control family.
